title: THE INDEX CAN HOLD UP WHILE THE STRUCTURE UNDERNEATH IT BREAKS
summary: Institutional capital is rotating through a market whose surface can remain elevated even while leadership, liquidity, and positioning fracture underneath it. Legacy technology holdings can be sold to fund the next layer of AI infrastructure while index construction and concentrated mega-cap weightings keep the headline market looking stronger than the capital structure beneath it. THE INDEX IS THE DISPLAY. THE CAPITAL MOVING UNDERNEATH IT IS THE STRUCTURE.
core_warning: A RISING INDEX IS NOT PROOF OF A HEALTHY MARKET.
INDEX STRENGTH CAN HIDE CAPITAL ROTATION.
CONCENTRATION CAN HOLD THE SURFACE UP WHILE LIQUIDITY DRAINS UNDERNEATH IT.
DEHEDGING CAN BEGIN BEFORE THE INDEX LOOKS BROKEN.
THE MARKET DOES NOT HAVE TO LOOK WEAK BEFORE ITS INTERNAL SUPPORT STARTS TO FAIL.
THE FOUNDATION CAN MOVE BEFORE THE SURFACE FALLS.

institutional_microstructure_shift.narrative: The danger is not simply that one index rises while another weakens. The danger is that concentrated index construction can delay the moment when the headline price finally reflects the stress already moving through the underlying market structure.

dehedging_cascade_parameters.warning: WHEN THE POSITIONING THAT HELD THE INDEX UP STARTS TO UNWIND, THE SAME MECHANICS THAT SUPPORTED THE SURFACE CAN ACCELERATE THE FALL.

index_rules_comparison.framework: Divergence in Mega-IPO Inclusion Criteria (S&P 500 vs Nasdaq-100)

sp_dow_jones_indices.strategic_effect: Keeps existing mega-cap technology weight concentrated inside the index while capital can continue moving into physical AI infrastructure. The headline index can therefore remain elevated even as the underlying allocation of capital changes dramatically.

nasdaq_omx_group.strategic_effect: A major new inclusion can force capital rotation across existing components, exposing how quickly apparent index stability can become a redistribution event inside the market itself.
